newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli tax revenue rose 3 pct in first 11 months.
newsitem.headline: Israeli tax revenue rose 3 pct in first 11 months.

text.p: Israeli government tax revenues rose three percent in real terms to 87.1 billion shekels in the first 11 months of the year, compared with the 1995 period, the Treasury said on Monday.

Revenues from income and property taxes were unchanged in real terms in the 11 months at 47.3 billion shekels, while revenue from value-addded tax and customs was up five percent to 38.6 billion shekels.

Tax revenues have fallen short of the amount forecast in the 1996 budget, which has helped to widen this year's deficit to an expected 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, one percentage point higher than targeted.
The November revenue figures, which the Treasury did not publish separately, will be a major factor in determining the exact size of the 1997 budget cuts it will be asking from the cabinet next week.
Officials expect the second round of cuts, on top of 4.9 billion shekels already slated, to be between 1.5 and 2.3 billion shekels.
